assessment.overall_rationale: The strongest correspondences are the shared tip-cell sprouting program and the narrower Kcnj2 mechanosensing module, while other pairs share only vascular context or secondary angiogenic outputs.

pair_scores.rationale: Both modules describe Angpt2/Cxcr4-driven brain endothelial tip-cell sprouting, with Nrp1–CDC42 activity and reduced Tek signaling promoting vascular network formation.
Both concern postnatal vascular adaptation, but tip-cell sprouting and Kcnj2-dependent flow sensing are distinct mechanisms and outputs.
Tnfrsf11b-mediated survival and angiogenic support overlap with vascular sprouting, but the right module emphasizes permissive metabolic and survival mechanisms rather than tip-cell specification.
The modules share Angpt2, Cxcr4, Rgs6, Tek, and arteriovenous patterning biology, but one centers identity specification while the other centers active tip-cell sprouting.
Arteriovenous identity specification and potassium-channel-mediated shear sensing share cerebrovascular context but not their central mechanism or predicted phenotype.
Endothelial survival and metabolic support can enable vascular remodeling, but they do not directly reproduce the arterial-versus-venous identity program.
BBB transport and flow sensing are distinct from tip-cell sprouting despite their common brain endothelial and vascular-development context.
The right module closely reproduces the Kcnj2-dependent shear-sensing and flow-induced vasodilation arm of the left module while omitting its BBB transport and TGF-beta components.
The modules share Slc1a1 and Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2, but assign them to different outputs—BBB glutamate homeostasis and integrity versus metabolic support of angiogenic remodeling.
